$comment: Plan 25 per-target struct variants — arm64-linux leg + the RED-ON-DISABLE pin. <sys/stat.h>'s `struct stat` (arch=arm64, format=elf) variant is the 128-byte glibc layout (DIVERGES from x86-64's 144), so `sizeof(struct stat)` folds to 128 → st_mode(40)+st_blocks(2)=42. Runs under qemu-aarch64 on the linux CI leg; cross-compiles locally. RED-ON-DISABLE: neuter the variant selector → arm64 gets the x86-64 144-byte variant → sizeof != 128 → exit 7. The release arm runs the optimizer over the struct shapes.

optimizedPipelines.$commentByteIdentical: MEASURED 2026-08-15 — optimized image BYTE-IDENTICAL to the baseline on: arm64:elf64-aarch64-linux-exec. Legs actually run: windows/pe64-x86_64 and linux/elf64 (x86_64 + aarch64 under qemu); the darwin/macho64 leg was NOT run. Where the image is identical the arm's exit-code/stdout comparison is x==x and cannot fail. HONEST: the values here live in an AGGREGATE (struct/union/array) local or global. The shipped pipeline does not promote aggregate storage, so the address-compute/store/load chain survives the pipeline unchanged. The two operands are members of a `struct stat` local. Deliberately NOT given "mustDifferFromBaseline" — an honest no-op, not a missed opt-in.
